Langkawi|Malaysia.f: One account traces the name to helang, the Malay word for eagle, and kawi, a red stone used as chalk to mark goods.

Phu Quoc|Vietnam.f: From 1953 to 1975 the island held South Vietnam's largest prisoner camp, with 40,000 inmates in 1973.

Panglao|Philippines.f: The Panglao watchtower, built in 1851, is a 5-storey octagonal tower and the tallest of its kind in the Philippines.

Ko Samui|Thailand.f: Bronze ritual drums etched with birds, boats and spirits found in the southern hills suggest people lived here 2,000 years ago.

Rota|N. Mariana Is..f: The first European to sight Rota was Lope Navarro, the lookout on Magellan's ship Victoria, in 1521.

Yap|Micronesia.f: Yapese society has at least seven tiers of rank, which froze in place under German rule, and villages keep the same rank today.

Kosrae|Micronesia.f: The city of Leluh on Kosrae thrived from about 1250 to 1850 AD, with some 1,500 people on about 27 hectares.

Neiafu|Tonga.f: Neiafu is Tonga's second largest town, and from May to October visitors can dive with humpback whales around Vava'u.

Biak|Indonesia.f: Biak lies about 1 degree south of the equator, so rockets launched from the island would need less fuel to reach orbit.

Hao|Fr. Polynesia.f: Explorer Louis Antoine de Bougainville named Hao atoll Ile de la Harpe, or Harp Island, because of its shape.

Labuan|Malaysia.f: Japanese occupiers renamed Labuan Maida Island on 9 December 1942.

Tinian|N. Mariana Is..f: The B-29s Enola Gay and Bockscar, which carried the atomic bombs, took off from North Field on Tinian.

Ranai|Indonesia.f: Indonesia opened a naval base with over 1,000 personnel on Natuna Besar, the island Ranai is on, on 18 December 2018.

Langgur|Indonesia.f: Langgur is the nominal capital of Southeast Maluku and sits across a tiny channel from the separate city of Tual.

Pangkal Pinang|Indonesia.f: Its name joins pengkal, meaning base, and pinang, the areca palm widely grown on Bangka island.

Tanjung Pinang|Indonesia.f: Tanjungpinang served as the capital of both the Johor Sultanate and the Riau-Lingga Sultanate.

Meekatharra|Australia.f: Meekatharra is a Yamatji word meaning place of little water.

Paraburdoo|Australia.f: Paraburdoo's all-time record high is 48.1 C, set on 21 January 2024.

Wangi-Wangi|Indonesia.f: The island is the seat of Wakatobi Regency and home to the Wangi-wangi white-eye, a recently discovered endangered bird.

Rangiroa|Fr. Polynesia.f: Rangiroa's lagoon covers 1,446 square km and is so large that it has its own horizon.

Leonora|Australia.f: Explorer John Forrest named Mount Leonora in 1869 after his six-year-old niece Frances Leonora Hardey.

Mangareva|Fr. Polynesia.f: Mangarevans counted in units of 10, 20, 40 and 80, writing 150 in four digits where binary needs eight.

Alyangula|Australia.f: Alyangula was built in the late 1960s by the Groote Eylandt Mining Company as a home for its workers.

Manus|Papua New Guinea.f: Anthropologist Margaret Mead lived on Manus before and after WWII and wrote Growing Up in New Guinea about it.

Con Dao|Vietnam.f: Ptolemy called these islands the Isles of the Satyrs, likely after the endemic long-tailed macaques living there.

Bourke|Australia.f: The first paddle steamer to reach Fort Bourke was the Genesis, skippered by Captain William Randell in February 1859.

Wiluna|Australia.f: Wiluna sits on the edge of the Western Desert at the gateway to the Canning Stock Route and the Gunbarrel Highway.

Leinster|Australia.f: Leinster was founded in 1976 by Agnew Mining as a dormitory town for miners at nearby nickel mines.

Mount Magnet|Australia.f: Magnetic north equals true north at Mount Magnet, where iron-rich hills once skewed explorer Robert Austin's compass.

Ternate|Indonesia.f: Ternate and Tidore were the world's major clove producers, making their sultans among the wealthiest in the region.

Ceduna|Australia.f: Ceduna is a Wirangu word, thought to mean a place to sit down and rest.

Cunnamulla|Australia.f: The town is named after Cunnamullah station, itself the Aboriginal name of a deep waterhole in the Warrego River.

Birdsville|Australia.f: The Birdsville Races add 7000 to 9000 people to the town, and hundreds of aircraft fill its 1,700 metre airstrip.

Barcaldine|Australia.f: Barcaldine's Tree of Knowledge, where 1891 shearers' strikers gathered, was poisoned with Roundup in 2006.

Nuku Hiva|Fr. Polynesia.f: Herman Melville based his novel Typee on his experiences in the Taipivai valley on Nuku Hiva.

Denham|Australia.f: Denham is the westernmost publicly accessible town in Australia, 831 km north of Perth.

Blackall|Australia.f: In 1892 Jackie Howe hand-sheared 321 sheep in 7 hours 40 minutes at Alice Downs near Blackall, a record that still stands.

Normanton|Australia.f: Normanton has a statue of Krys, an 8.64 metre saltwater crocodile shot in the Norman River in 1957.

Walgett|Australia.f: Walgett is the gateway to the New South Wales opal fields at Lightning Ridge and The Grawin.

Kaimana|Indonesia.f: Bryde's whales visit the waters near Kaimana, including Triton Bay.
